	<us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock contextRef="FD2019Q1YTD" id="Fact-5AE96E8B6DCA5084A23C391101B74E9A">&lt;div style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;color:#000000;font-weight:bold;text-decoration:none;"&gt;Fair Value Measurements&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt; &lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Recurring Fair Value Measurements&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We carry certain assets and liabilities at fair value, which we measure at the reporting date using the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability (i.e., an exit price), and disclose the quality of these fair values based on the valuation inputs used in these measurements under the following hierarchy:&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;padding-left:48px;text-indent:-24px;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8226;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Level 1: Fair value measured with unadjusted quoted prices from an active market for identical assets or liabilities.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8226;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Level 2: Fair value measured either with: (1) adjusted quoted prices from an active market for similar assets or liabilities; or (2) other valuation inputs that are directly or indirectly observable.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8226;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Level 3: Fair value measured with unobservable inputs that are significant to the measurement.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;padding-left:48px;text-indent:-24px;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We classify the fair value of an asset or liability based on the significance of its observable or unobservable inputs to the measurement.  However, the fair value of an asset or liability initially reported as Level 3 will be subsequently reported as Level 2 if the unobservable inputs become inconsequential to its measurement or corroborating market data becomes available.  Conversely, an asset or liability initially reported as Level 2 will be subsequently reported as Level 3 if corroborating market data becomes unavailable.  For the &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;three months ended&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;March&amp;#160;31, 2019&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, derivative assets with an aggregate value of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;$53 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; and derivative liabilities with an aggregate value of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;$22 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; were transferred to Level 1 from Level 2, as measured from the beginning of the reporting period.  The measurements were reclassified within the fair value hierarchy due to the availability of unadjusted quoted prices from an active market.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We used the following methods and assumptions to estimate the fair value of financial instruments:&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8226;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Cash and cash equivalents&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8212;The carrying amount reported on our consolidated balance sheet approximates fair value.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8226;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Accounts and notes receivable&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8212;The carrying amount reported on our consolidated balance sheet approximates fair value.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8226;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Derivative instruments&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8212;We fair value our exchange-traded contracts based on quoted market prices obtained from the New York Mercantile Exchange, the Intercontinental Exchange or other exchanges, and classify them as Level 1 in the fair value hierarchy.  When exchange-cleared contracts lack sufficient liquidity, or are valued using either adjusted exchange-provided prices or non-exchange quotes, we classify those contracts as Level 2.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:6px;text-align:left;padding-left:48px;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Physical commodity forward purchase and sales contracts and over-the-counter (OTC) financial swaps are generally valued using forward quotes provided by brokers and price index developers, such as Platts and Oil Price Information Service. We corroborate these quotes with market data and classify the resulting fair values as Level 2.  When forward market prices are not available, we estimate fair value using the forward price of a similar commodity, adjusted for the difference in quality or location.  In certain less liquid markets or for longer-term contracts, forward prices are not as readily available.  In these circumstances, physical commodity purchase and sales contracts and OTC swaps are valued using internally developed methodologies that consider historical relationships among various commodities that result in management&amp;#8217;s best estimate of fair value.  We classify these contracts as Level 3.  Physical and OTC commodity options are valued using industry-standard models that consider various assumptions, including quoted forward prices for commodities, time value, volatility factors and contractual prices for the underlying instruments, as well as other relevant economic measures.  The degree to which these inputs are observable in the forward markets determines whether the options are classified as Level 2 or 3.  We use a mid-market pricing convention (the mid-point between bid and ask prices).  When appropriate, valuations are adjusted to reflect credit considerations, generally based on available market evidence.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:6px;text-align:left;padding-left:48px;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We determine the fair value of our interest rate swaps based on observed market valuations for interest rate swaps that have notional amounts, terms and pay and reset frequencies similar to ours.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8226;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Rabbi trust assets&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8212;These deferred compensation investments are measured at fair value using unadjusted quoted prices available from national securities exchanges and are therefore categorized as Level 1 in the fair value hierarchy.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8226;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Debt&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8212;The carrying amount of our floating-rate debt approximates fair value.  The fair value of our fixed-rate debt is estimated based on observable market prices.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;The following tables display the fair value hierarchy for our financial assets and liabilities either accounted for or disclosed at fair value on a recurring basis.  These values are determined by treating each contract as the fundamental unit of account; therefore, derivative assets and liabilities with the same counterparty are shown on a gross basis in the hierarchy sections of these tables, before the effects of counterparty and collateral netting.  The following tables also reflect the effect of netting derivative assets and liabilities with the same counterparty for which we have the legal right of offset and collateral netting.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br 	<us-gaap:FairValueOfFinancialInstrumentsPolicy contextRef="FD2019Q1YTD" id="Fact-4E76F19F1B9656C991DBCAD4CC1FD9AC">&lt;div style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Recurring Fair Value Measurements&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We carry certain assets and liabilities at fair value, which we measure at the reporting date using the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability (i.e., an exit price), and disclose the quality of these fair values based on the valuation inputs used in these measurements under the following hierarchy:&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;padding-left:48px;text-indent:-24px;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8226;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Level 1: Fair value measured with unadjusted quoted prices from an active market for identical assets or liabilities.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8226;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Level 2: Fair value measured either with: (1) adjusted quoted prices from an active market for similar assets or liabilities; or (2) other valuation inputs that are directly or indirectly observable.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8226;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Level 3: Fair value measured with unobservable inputs that are significant to the measurement.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;padding-left:48px;text-indent:-24px;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We classify the fair value of an asset or liability based on the significance of its observable or unobservable inputs to the measurement.  However, the fair value of an asset or liability initially reported as Level 3 will be subsequently reported as Level 2 if the unobservable inputs become inconsequential to its measurement or corroborating market data becomes available.  Conversely, an asset or liability initially reported as Level 2 will be subsequently reported as Level 3 if corroborating market data becomes unavailable.  For the &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;three months ended&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;March&amp;#160;31, 2019&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, derivative assets with an aggregate value of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;$53 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; and derivative liabilities with an aggregate value of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;$22 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; were transferred to Level 1 from Level 2, as measured from the beginning of the reporting period.  The measurements were reclassified within the fair value hierarchy due to the availability of unadjusted quoted prices from an active market.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We used the following methods and assumptions to estimate the fair value of financial instruments:&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8226;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Cash and cash equivalents&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8212;The carrying amount reported on our consolidated balance sheet approximates fair value.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8226;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Accounts and notes receivable&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8212;The carrying amount reported on our consolidated balance sheet approximates fair value.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8226;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Derivative instruments&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8212;We fair value our exchange-traded contracts based on quoted market prices obtained from the New York Mercantile Exchange, the Intercontinental Exchange or other exchanges, and classify them as Level 1 in the fair value hierarchy.  When exchange-cleared contracts lack sufficient liquidity, or are valued using either adjusted exchange-provided prices or non-exchange quotes, we classify those contracts as Level 2.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:6px;text-align:left;padding-left:48px;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Physical commodity forward purchase and sales contracts and over-the-counter (OTC) financial swaps are generally valued using forward quotes provided by brokers and price index developers, such as Platts and Oil Price Information Service. We corroborate these quotes with market data and classify the resulting fair values as Level 2.  When forward market prices are not available, we estimate fair value using the forward price of a similar commodity, adjusted for the difference in quality or location.  In certain less liquid markets or for longer-term contracts, forward prices are not as readily available.  In these circumstances, physical commodity purchase and sales contracts and OTC swaps are valued using internally developed methodologies that consider historical relationships among various commodities that result in management&amp;#8217;s best estimate of fair value.  We classify these contracts as Level 3.  Physical and OTC commodity options are valued using industry-standard models that consider various assumptions, including quoted forward prices for commodities, time value, volatility factors and contractual prices for the underlying instruments, as well as other relevant economic measures.  The degree to which these inputs are observable in the forward markets determines whether the options are classified as Level 2 or 3.  We use a mid-market pricing convention (the mid-point between bid and ask prices).  When appropriate, valuations are adjusted to reflect credit considerations, generally based on available market evidence.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:6px;text-align:left;padding-left:48px;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We determine the fair value of our interest rate swaps based on observed market valuations for interest rate swaps that have notional amounts, terms and pay and reset frequencies similar to ours.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8226;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Rabbi trust assets&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8212;These deferred compensation investments are measured at fair value using unadjusted quoted prices available from national securities exchanges and are therefore categorized as Level 1 in the fair value hierarchy.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:6px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:48px;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:24px;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8226;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Debt&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#8212;The carrying amount of our floating-rate debt approximates fair value.  The fair value of our fixed-rate debt is estimated based on observable market prices.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</us-gaap:FairValueOfFinancialInstrumentsPolicy>

We recognize a liability for the fair value of our obligation as a guarantor for newly issued or modified guarantees.  Unless the carrying amount of the liability is noted below, we have not recognized a liability either because the guarantees were issued prior to December&amp;#160;31, 2002, or because the fair value of the obligation is immaterial.  In addition, unless otherwise stated, we are not currently performing with any significance under the guarantees and expect future performance to be either immaterial or have only a remote chance of occurrence.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Guarantees of Joint Venture Obligations&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;At &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;March&amp;#160;31, 2019&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, we had guarantees outstanding for our portion of certain joint venture debt and purchase obligations, which have remaining terms of up to &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;seven&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; years.  The maximum potential amount of future payments to third parties under these guarantees was approximately &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;$207 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;.  Payment would be required if a joint venture defaults on its obligations.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Residual Value Guarantees&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Under the operating lease agreement on our headquarters facility in Houston, Texas, we have a residual value guarantee with a maximum future exposure of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;$554 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;.  The operating lease term ends in &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;June 2021&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; and provides us the option, at the end of the lease term, to request to renew the lease, purchase the facility or assist the lessor in marketing it for resale.  We also have residual value guarantees associated with railcar and airplane leases with maximum future exposures totaling &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;$288 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, which have remaining terms of up to &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;five&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; years.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Indemnifications&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Over the years, we have entered into various agreements to sell ownership interests in certain corporations, joint ventures and assets that gave rise to indemnification.  Agreements associated with these sales include indemnifications for taxes, litigation, environmental liabilities, permits and licenses and employee claims, as well as real estate indemnity against tenant defaults.  The provisions of these indemnifications vary greatly.  The majority of these indemnifications are related to environmental issues, which generally have indefinite terms and potentially unlimited exposure.  At &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;March&amp;#160;31, 2019&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, the carrying amount of recorded indemnifications was &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;$173 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;$171 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, respectively.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We amortize the indemnification liability over the relevant time period, if one exists, based on the facts and circumstances surrounding each type of indemnity.  In cases where the indemnification term is indefinite, we will reverse the liability when we have information to support that the liability was essentially relieved or amortize the liability over an appropriate time period as the fair value of our indemnification exposure declines.  Although it is reasonably possible future payments may exceed amounts recorded, due to the nature of the indemnifications, it is not possible to make a reasonable estimate of the maximum potential amount of future payments.  At &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;March&amp;#160;31, 2019&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;December&amp;#160;31, 2018&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, environmental accruals for known contamination of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;$104 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; and &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;$101 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, respectively, were included in the carrying amount of recorded indemnifications.  These environmental accruals were primarily included in the &amp;#8220;Asset retirement obligations and accrued environmental costs&amp;#8221; line on our consolidated balance sheet.  For additional information about environmental liabilities, see &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Note 11&amp;#8212;Contingencies and Commitments&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Indemnification and Release Agreement&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;In 2012, in connection with our separation from ConocoPhillips (the Separation), we entered into the Indemnification and Release Agreement.  This agreement governs the treatment between ConocoPhillips and us of matters relating to indemnification, insurance, litigation responsibility and management, and litigation document sharing and cooperation arising in connection with the Separation.  Generally, the agreement provides for cross-indemnities principally designed to place financial responsibility for the obligations and liabilities of our business with us and financial responsibility for the obligations and liabilities of ConocoPhillips&amp;#8217; business with ConocoPhillips.  The agreement also establishes procedures for handling claims subject to indemnification and related matters.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</us-gaap:GuaranteesTextBlock>

	<us-gaap:LesseeFinanceLeasesTextBlock contextRef="FD2019Q1YTD" id="Fact-0708980D66825DFA184745DBD45BB8A9">&lt;div style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Leases&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We lease marine vessels, tugboats, barges, pipelines, storage tanks, railcars, service station sites, office buildings, corporate aircraft, land and other facilities and equipment.  In determining whether an agreement contains a lease, we consider our ability to control the asset and whether there are limitations on our control through third-party participation or vendor substitution rights.  Certain leases include escalation clauses for adjusting rental payments to reflect changes in price indices, as well as renewal options and/or options to purchase the leased property.  Renewal options have been included only when reasonably certain of exercise.  There are no significant restrictions imposed on us in our lease agreements with regards to dividend payments, asset dispositions or borrowing ability.  Certain leases have residual value guarantees, which may require additional payments at the end of the lease term if future fair values decline below contractual lease balances.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;In our implementation of ASU No. 2016-02, we elected to discount lease obligations using our incremental borrowing rate.  Furthermore, we elected to separate costs for lease and service components for contracts involving the following asset types: marine vessels, tugboats, barges and consignment service stations.  For these contracts, we allocate the consideration payable between the lease and service components using the relative standalone prices of each component.  For contracts involving all other asset types, we elected the practical expedient to account for the lease and service components on a combined basis.  Our right-of-way agreements in effect prior to January 1, 2019, were not accounted for as leases as they were not initially determined to be leases at their commencement dates.  However, modifications to these agreements or new agreements will be assessed and accounted for accordingly under ASU No. 2016-02.  For short-term leases, which are leases that, at the commencement date, have a lease term of 12 months or less and do not include an option to purchase the underlying asset that is reasonably certain to exercise, we elected to not recognize the ROU asset and corresponding lease liability on our consolidated balance sheet.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;The following table indicates the consolidated balance sheet line items that include the ROU assets and lease liabilities for our finance and operating leases: &lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;div 	<us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeasesTextBlock contextRef="FD2019Q1YTD" id="Fact-F0FD6FF356030FF66F68FD3E3B9A4D29">&lt;div style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Leases&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We lease marine vessels, tugboats, barges, pipelines, storage tanks, railcars, service station sites, office buildings, corporate aircraft, land and other facilities and equipment.  In determining whether an agreement contains a lease, we consider our ability to control the asset and whether there are limitations on our control through third-party participation or vendor substitution rights.  Certain leases include escalation clauses for adjusting rental payments to reflect changes in price indices, as well as renewal options and/or options to purchase the leased property.  Renewal options have been included only when reasonably certain of exercise.  There are no significant restrictions imposed on us in our lease agreements with regards to dividend payments, asset dispositions or borrowing ability.  Certain leases have residual value guarantees, which may require additional payments at the end of the lease term if future fair values decline below contractual lease balances.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;In our implementation of ASU No. 2016-02, we elected to discount lease obligations using our incremental borrowing rate.  Furthermore, we elected to separate costs for lease and service components for contracts involving the following asset types: marine vessels, tugboats, barges and consignment service stations.  For these contracts, we allocate the consideration payable between the lease and service components using the relative standalone prices of each component.  For contracts involving all other asset types, we elected the practical expedient to account for the lease and service components on a combined basis.  Our right-of-way agreements in effect prior to January 1, 2019, were not accounted for as leases as they were not initially determined to be leases at their commencement dates.  However, modifications to these agreements or new agreements will be assessed and accounted for accordingly under ASU No. 2016-02.  For short-term leases, which are leases that, at the commencement date, have a lease term of 12 months or less and do not include an option to purchase the underlying asset that is reasonably certain to exercise, we elected to not recognize the ROU asset and corresponding lease liability on our consolidated balance sheet.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;The following table indicates the consolidated balance sheet line items that include the ROU assets and lease liabilities for our finance and operating leases: &lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:center;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;div Activities&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;For the &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font of common units, or at-the-market (ATM) programs.  Since inception in June 2016 through &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;March&amp;#160;31, 2019&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, the ATM programs generated net proceeds of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;$352 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Phillips 66 Partners holds an investment in the Gray Oak Pipeline through Holdings LLC.  In December 2018, a third party exercised its option to acquire a &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;35%&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; interest in Holdings LLC.  Because Holdings LLC&amp;#8217;s sole asset was its ownership interest in Gray Oak, which is considered a financial asset, and because certain restrictions were placed on the third party&amp;#8217;s ability to transfer or sell its interest in Holdings LLC during the construction of the Gray Oak Pipeline, the legal sale of the &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;35%&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; interest did not qualify as a sale under GAAP.  As such, the contributions the third party is making to Holdings LLC to cover its share of previously incurred and future construction costs plus a premium to Phillips 66 Partners are reflected as a long-term obligation in the &amp;#8220;Other liabilities and deferred credits&amp;#8221; line on our consolidated balance sheet and financing cash inflows in the &amp;#8220;Other&amp;#8221; line on our consolidated statement of cash flows.  The sale will be recognized under GAAP after construction of the Gray Oak Pipeline is completed and the restrictions expire.  Phillips 66 Partners will continue to control and consolidate Holdings LLC after sale recognition, and therefore the third party&amp;#8217;s &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;35%&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; interest will be recharacterized from a long-term obligation to a noncontrolling interest on our consolidated balance sheet at that time.  Also at that time, the premium paid will be recharacterized from a long-term obligation to a gain in our consolidated statement of income.  For the &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;three months ended&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;March&amp;#160;31, 2019&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, the third party contributed an aggregate of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;$341 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; into Holdings LLC, which Holdings LLC used to fund its portion of Gray Oak&amp;#8217;s cash calls.  See &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Note 6&amp;#8212;Investments, Loans and Long-Term Receivables&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, for further discussion regarding Phillip 66 Partners&amp;#8217; investment in Gray Oak.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</us-gaap:MinorityInterestDisclosureTextBlock>
	<us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock contextRef="FD2019Q1YTD" id="Fact-CBDFFD99B73B5A978060033B0CFDDFC1">&lt;div style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Changes in Accounting Principles&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt; &lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Effective January 1, 2019, we elected to adopt Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) Accounting Standards Update (ASU) No. 2018-02, &amp;#8220;Income Statement&amp;#8212;Reporting Comprehensive Income (Topic 220): Reclassification of Certain Tax Effects from Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income.&amp;#8221;  This ASU permits the deferred income tax effects stranded in accumulated other comprehensive income (AOCI) resulting from the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (the Tax Act) enacted in December 2017 to be reclassified to retained earnings.  As of January 1, 2019, we recorded a cumulative effect adjustment to our opening consolidated balance sheet to reclassify an aggregate income tax benefit of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;$89 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, primarily related to our pension plans, from accumulated other comprehensive loss to retained earnings. &lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Effective January 1, 2019, we early adopted ASU 2016-13, &amp;#8220;Financial Instruments&amp;#8212;Credit Losses (Topic 326):  Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments,&amp;#8221; using the modified retrospective transition method.  This ASU amends the impairment model to utilize an expected loss methodology in place of the incurred loss methodology for financial instruments, including trade receivables, and off-balance sheet credit exposures.  The amendment requires entities to consider a broader range of information to estimate expected credit losses, which may result in earlier recognition of losses.  We recorded a noncash cumulative effect adjustment to retained earnings of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;$9 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, net of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;$3 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; of income taxes, on our opening consolidated balance sheet as of January 1, 2019.  See &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Note 4&amp;#8212;Credit Losses&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, for more information on our presentation of credit losses.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Effective January 1, 2019, we adopted ASU No. 2016-02, &amp;#8220;Leases (Topic 842),&amp;#8221; using the modified retrospective transition method.  The new standard establishes a right-of-use (ROU) model that requires a lessee to record a ROU asset and a lease liability on the consolidated balance sheet for all leases with terms longer than 12 months.  Leases will continue to be classified as either finance or operating, with classification affecting the pattern of expense recognition in the consolidated income statement.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;br clear="none"/&gt;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We elected the package of practical expedients that allowed us to carry forward our determination of whether an arrangement contained a lease and lease classification, as well as our accounting for initial direct costs for existing contracts.  We recorded a noncash cumulative effect adjustment to our opening consolidated balance sheet as of January 1, 2019, to record an aggregate operating lease ROU asset and corresponding lease liability of &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;$1,415 million&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt; and immaterial adjustments to retained earnings and noncontrolling interests.  See &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;Note 14&amp;#8212;Leases&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;, for the new lease disclosures required by this ASU.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock>

We also paid fees to various pipeline affiliates for transporting crude oil, refined petroleum products and NGL.  &lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-left:4px;text-align:left;padding-left:36px;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&amp;#160;&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:36px;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;padding-left:0px;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;(c)&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;We paid utility and processing fees to various affiliates.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</us-gaap:RelatedPartyTransactionsDisclosureTextBlock>

These borrowings were subsequently refinanced through a public offering of senior notes in March 2018.  This specific share repurchase transaction was separately authorized by our Board of Directors and therefore does not impact previously announced authorizations to repurchase shares of Phillips 66 common stock under our share repurchase program, which total up to &lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;$12 billion&lt;/font&gt;&lt;font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"&gt;.&lt;/font&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</us-gaap:TreasuryStockTextBlock>

<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Total of all stockholders' equity (deficit) items, net of receivables from officers, directors, owners, and affiliates of the entity which are attributable to the parent. The amount of the economic entity's stockholders' equity attributable to the parent excludes the amount of stockholders' equity which is allocable to that ownership interest in subsidiary equity which is not attributable to the parent (noncontrolling interest, minority interest). This excludes temporary equity and is sometimes called permanent equity.</p></div>

<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_AccountingChangesTextBlock', window );">Changes in Accounting Principles</a></td>
<td class="text"><div style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;">Changes in Accounting Principles</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;"> </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br clear="none"/></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">Effective January 1, 2019, we elected to adopt Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) Accounting Standards Update (ASU) No. 2018-02, &#8220;Income Statement&#8212;Reporting Comprehensive Income (Topic 220): Reclassification of Certain Tax Effects from Accumulated Other Comprehensive Income.&#8221;  This ASU permits the deferred income tax effects stranded in accumulated other comprehensive income (AOCI) resulting from the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (the Tax Act) enacted in December 2017 to be reclassified to retained earnings.  As of January 1, 2019, we recorded a cumulative effect adjustment to our opening consolidated balance sheet to reclassify an aggregate income tax benefit of </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$89 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, primarily related to our pension plans, from accumulated other comprehensive loss to retained earnings. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br clear="none"/></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">Effective January 1, 2019, we early adopted ASU 2016-13, &#8220;Financial Instruments&#8212;Credit Losses (Topic 326):  Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments,&#8221; using the modified retrospective transition method.  This ASU amends the impairment model to utilize an expected loss methodology in place of the incurred loss methodology for financial instruments, including trade receivables, and off-balance sheet credit exposures.  The amendment requires entities to consider a broader range of information to estimate expected credit losses, which may result in earlier recognition of losses.  We recorded a noncash cumulative effect adjustment to retained earnings of </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$9 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, net of </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$3 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> of income taxes, on our opening consolidated balance sheet as of January 1, 2019.  See </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">Note 4&#8212;Credit Losses</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, for more information on our presentation of credit losses.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br clear="none"/></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">Effective January 1, 2019, we adopted ASU No. 2016-02, &#8220;Leases (Topic 842),&#8221; using the modified retrospective transition method.  The new standard establishes a right-of-use (ROU) model that requires a lessee to record a ROU asset and a lease liability on the consolidated balance sheet for all leases with terms longer than 12 months.  Leases will continue to be classified as either finance or operating, with classification affecting the pattern of expense recognition in the consolidated income statement.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br clear="none"/></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">We elected the package of practical expedients that allowed us to carry forward our determination of whether an arrangement contained a lease and lease classification, as well as our accounting for initial direct costs for existing contracts.  We recorded a noncash cumulative effect adjustment to our opening consolidated balance sheet as of January 1, 2019, to record an aggregate operating lease ROU asset and corresponding lease liability of </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$1,415 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> and immaterial adjustments to retained earnings and noncontrolling interests.  See </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">Note 14&#8212;Leases</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, for the new lease disclosures required by this ASU.</font></div></div><span></span>
</td>
</tr>
</table>

An incentive payment is initially recognized as an asset and subsequently amortized as a reduction to revenue over the contract term, which generally ranges from </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">5</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> to </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">15</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> years.  At </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">March&#160;31, 2019</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, and </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">December&#160;31, 2018</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, our asset balances related to such payments were </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$259 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> and </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$248 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, respectively. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br clear="none"/></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">Our contract liabilities represent advances from our customers prior to product or service delivery. We do not disclose remaining performance obligations for these contracts as the expected duration is one year or less or because the variable consideration has been allocated entirely to an unsatisfied performance obligation.  We also have certain contracts in our Midstream segment that include minimum volume commitments with fixed pricing, most of which expire by 2021.  At </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">March&#160;31, 2019</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, the remaining performance obligations related to these minimum volume commitment contracts were not material.</font></div></div><span></span>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure of revenue from contract with customer to transfer good or service and to transfer nonfinancial asset. Includes, but is not limited to, disaggregation of revenue, credit loss recognized from contract with customer, judgment and change in judgment related to contract with customer, and asset recognized from cost incurred to obtain or fulfill contract with customer. Excludes insurance and lease contracts.</p></div>

<th class="th" colspan="1">3 Months Ended</th>

<tr><th class="th"><div>Mar. 31, 2019</div></th></tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLossAdditionalInformationAbstract', window );"><strong>Financing Receivable, Allowance for Credit Loss, Additional Information [Abstract]</strong></a></td>
<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_AllowanceForCreditLossesTextBlock', window );">Credit Losses</a></td>
<td class="text"><div style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;">Credit Losses</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">We are exposed to credit losses primarily through our sales of refined petroleum products, crude oil and NGLs.  We assess each counterparty&#8217;s ability to pay for the products we sell by conducting a credit review.  The credit review considers our expected billing exposure and timing for payment and the counterparty&#8217;s established credit rating or our assessment of the counterparty&#8217;s creditworthiness based on our analysis of their financial statements when a credit rating is not available.  We also consider contract terms and conditions, country and political risk, and business strategy in our evaluation.  A credit limit is established for each counterparty based on the outcome of this review.  We may require collateralized asset support or a prepayment to mitigate credit risk.  </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br clear="none"/></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">We monitor our ongoing credit exposure through active review of counterparty balances against contract terms and due dates.  Our activities include timely account reconciliation, dispute resolution and payment confirmation.  We may employ collection agencies and legal counsel to pursue recovery of defaulted receivables.  </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br clear="none"/></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">At </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">March&#160;31, 2019</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, we reported </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$7,303 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> of accounts receivable, net of allowances of </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$35 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.  Changes in the allowance were not material for the </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">three months</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> ended </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">March&#160;31, 2019</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.  Based on an aging analysis at </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">March&#160;31, 2019</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">99%</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> of our accounts receivable were outstanding less than 60 days, with the remainder outstanding less than 90 days.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br clear="none"/></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">We are also exposed to credit losses from off-balance sheet exposures, such as guarantees of joint venture debt, residual value guarantees of leased assets and standby letters of credit.  See </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">Note 10&#8212;Guarantees</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, and </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">Note 11&#8212;Contingencies and Commitments</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, for more information on these off-balance sheet exposures.</font></div></div><span></span>
</td>
</tr>

#000000;background-color:#cceeff;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"><div style="text-align:right;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">378</font></div></td><td style="vertical-align:bottom;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;background-color:#cceeff;" rowspan="1" colspan="1"><div style="text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br clear="none"/></font></div></td></tr></table></div><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br clear="none"/></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br clear="none"/></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br clear="none"/></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;text-decoration:underline;">Dakota Access, LLC (Dakota Access) and Energy Transfer Crude Oil Company, LLC (ETCO)</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">In March 2019, a wholly owned subsidiary of Dakota Access closed on an offering of </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$2,500 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> aggregate principal amount of unsecured senior notes.  The net proceeds from the issuance of these notes were used to repay amounts outstanding under existing credit facilities of Dakota Access and ETCO.  Dakota Access and ETCO have guaranteed repayment of the notes.  In addition, Phillips 66 Partners LP (Phillips 66 Partners) and its co-venturers provided a Contingent Equity Contribution Undertaking (CECU) in conjunction with the notes offering.  Under the CECU, if Dakota Access receives an unfavorable court ruling related to certain disputed construction permits and Dakota Access determines that an equity contribution trigger event has occurred, the venturers may be severally required to make proportionate equity contributions to Dakota Access and ETCO up to an aggregate maximum of approximately </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$2,525 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.  Phillips 66 Partners&#8217; share of the maximum potential equity contributions under the CECU is approximately </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$631 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br clear="none"/></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;text-decoration:underline;">Gray Oak Pipeline, LLC (Gray Oak)</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">In February 2019, Gray Oak Holdings LLC (Holdings LLC), a consolidated subsidiary of Phillips 66 Partners, transferred a </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">10%</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> ownership interest in Gray Oak to a third party that exercised a purchase option for proceeds of </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$81 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.  This transfer was accounted for as a sale and resulted in a decrease in Holdings LLC&#8217;s ownership interest in Gray Oak from </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">75%</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> to </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">65%</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> and the recognition of an immaterial gain.  The proceeds received from this sale are presented as an investing cash inflow in the &#8220;Proceeds from asset dispositions&#8221; line on our consolidated statement of cash flows.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br clear="none"/></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">Phillips 66 Partners accounts for the investment in Gray Oak under the equity method because it does not have sufficient voting rights over key governance provisions to assert control over Gray Oak.  Gray Oak is considered a variable interest entity (VIE) because it does not have sufficient equity at risk to fully fund the construction of all assets required for principal operations.  Phillips 66 Partners has determined it is not the primary beneficiary because it and its co-venturers jointly direct the activities of Gray Oak that most significantly impact economic performance.  At </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">March&#160;31, 2019</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, Phillips 66 Partners&#8217; maximum exposure to loss was </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$771 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, which represented the book value of the investment in Gray Oak of </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$741 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> and guaranteed purchase obligations of </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$30 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br clear="none"/></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-left:4px;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">See </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">Note 21&#8212;Phillips 66 Partners LP</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, for additional information regarding Phillips 66 Partners&#8217; ownership in Holdings LLC and Gray Oak.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br clear="none"/></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-left:4px;text-align:left;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;text-decoration:underline;">OnCue Holdings, LLC (OnCue)</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-left:4px;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">We hold a </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">50%</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> interest in OnCue, a joint venture that owns and operates retail convenience stores.  We fully guaranteed various debt agreements of OnCue and our co-venturer did not participate in the guarantees.  This entity is considered a VIE because our debt guarantees resulted in OnCue not being exposed to all potential losses.  We have determined we are not the primary beneficiary because we do not have the power to direct the activities that most significantly impact economic performance.  At </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">March&#160;31, 2019</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, our maximum exposure to loss was </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$124 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, which represented the book value of our investment in OnCue of </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$70 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> and guaranteed debt obligations of </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$54 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;font-weight:bold;">Related Party Loan</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"><br clear="none"/></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10.5pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">On </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">March&#160;29, 2019</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, Phillips 66 Partners and its co-venturers executed an agreement to loan Gray Oak up to a maximum of </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$1,230 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> to finance construction of the Gray Oak Pipeline.  The amount loaned by each venturer is expected to be proportionate to its effective ownership interest.  The maximum amount to be loaned by Phillips 66 Partners is </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$520 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.  Loans under this agreement are due on </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">March&#160;31, 2022</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, with early repayment permitted.  On </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">April&#160;1, 2019</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">, Phillips 66 Partners and its co-venturers loaned Gray Oak a total of </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$125 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;"> under this agreement, of which Phillips 66 Partners&#8217; share was </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">$53 million</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10.5pt;">.</font></div></div><span></span>

<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for equity method investments and joint ventures. Equity method investments are investments that give the investor the ability to exercise significant influence over the operating and financial policies of an investee. Joint ventures are entities owned and operated by a small group of businesses as a separate and specific business or project for the mutual benefit of the members of the group.</p></div>
